simple_meaning: A protein inside red blood cells that carries oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body.
The average size of your red blood cells.
A blood protein that reflects how much iron is stored in your body.
White blood cells (leukocytes), which are part of your body's immune response.
Tiny cell fragments in blood that help form clots to stop bleeding.
An essential mineral (electrolyte) that helps nerves, muscles, and the heart beat properly.
An electrolyte that helps balance water levels in your body and supports nerve and muscle function.
A normal muscle waste product filtered out of your blood by your kidneys.
An estimate of how well your kidneys are filtering blood each minute.
A blood test showing your average blood sugar level over the past 2 to 3 months.
The amount of sugar in your blood after not eating or drinking anything except water for at least 8 hours.
A type of cholesterol-carrying particle often monitored because high levels can build up in blood vessels over time.
A cholesterol-carrying particle that helps clear other forms of cholesterol from the bloodstream.
A common type of fat found in the blood that the body uses for energy.
A protein released into the blood when heart muscle cells are stressed or injured.
A standardized measurement of how quickly your blood forms a clot.
The span of values typically seen in most healthy people tested by that laboratory.
